verses.sanskrit:
लोमश उवाच।
              इह मर्त्यास्तनूस्त्यक्त्वा स्वर्गं गच्छन्ति भारत। मर्तुकामा नरा राजन्निहायान्ति सहस्त्रशः॥१॥
verses.english: Lomasha said: O descendant of Bharata, if men give up their bodies here, they go to heaven. O king, thousands of men come here with the desire to die.

verses.sanskrit: एवमाशीः प्रयुक्ता हि दक्षेण यजता पुरा। इह ये वै मरिष्यन्ति ते वै स्वर्गजितो नराः॥२॥
verses.english: A blessing was pronounced here by Daksha when in the days of yore he was performing sacrifice at this spot. (It was as follows), “The men that will die here will go to heaven.”

verses.sanskrit: एषा सरस्वती रम्या दिव्या चौघवती नदी। एतद्विनशनं नाम सरस्वत्या विशांपते॥३॥
verses.english: O king, here is the charming celestials river full of water, named Sarasvati. It is here Vinasana of the Sarasvati (where she disappeared).

verses.sanskrit: द्वारं निषादराष्ट्रस्य येषां दोषात्सरस्वती। प्रविष्टा पृथिवीं वीर मा निषादा हि मां विदुः॥४॥
verses.english: O hero, here is the gate of the kingdom of the Nishadas; it is from the hatred of the Nishadhas that the Sarasvati entered the earth so that she might not be seen by the Nishadas.

verses.sanskrit: एष वै चमसोद्भेदो यत्र दृश्या सरस्वती। यत्रैनामभ्यवर्तन्त सर्वाः पुण्याः समुद्रगाः॥५॥
verses.english: Here is also Chamashodbheda where the Sarasvati again reappeared. Here she was joined by all the other sacred ocean-going currents.

verses.sanskrit: एतत्सिन्धोर्महत्तीर्थं यत्रागस्त्यमरिंदम। लोपामुद्रा समागम्य भर्तारमवृणीत वै॥६॥
verses.english: O chastiser of foes, here is the greatly sacred place called Sindhu, where Lopamudra accepted the great Rishi Agastya as her husband.

verses.sanskrit: एतत्प्रकाशते तीर्थं प्रभासं भास्करद्युते। इन्द्रस्य दयितं पुण्यं पवित्रं पापनाशनम्॥७॥
verses.english: O sun-like effulgent hero, here is the sacred Tirtha called Pravasha which is truly sacred, sin-destroying and a favourite place of Indra.

verses.sanskrit: एतद्विष्णुपदं नाम दृश्यते तीर्थमुत्तमम्। एषा रम्या विपाशा च नदी परमपावनी॥८॥
verses.english: Yonder appears the excellent Tirtha called Vishnupada. Here also is the charming river and greatly purifying Vipasa.

verses.sanskrit: अत्र वै पुत्रशोकेन वसिष्ठो भगवानृषिः। बद्ध्वात्मानं निपतितो विपाशः पुनरुत्थितः॥९॥
verses.english: Here from the grief at his son's death, the great Rishi Vasishtha threw himself into the Vipasa after first binding himself, but he rose again.

verses.sanskrit: काश्मीरमण्डलं चैतत्सर्वपुण्यमरिंदम। महर्षिभिश्चाध्युषितं पश्येदं भ्रातृभिः सह॥१०॥
verses.english: O chastiser of foes, behold with your brothers the sacred region of Kashmira, ever frequented by the holy Rishis.
verses.bhavadeepa: बद्ध्वा पाशैरिति शेषः । विपाशः पाशहीनः । अत एव विपाशा नाम ॥९॥

verses.sanskrit: यत्रौत्तराणां सर्वेषामृषीणां नाहुषस्य च। अग्नेश्चैवात्र संवादः काश्यपस्य च भारत॥११॥
verses.english: O descendant of Bharata, here a conference took place between Agni and the Rishi Kashyapa and between the son of Nahusha (Yayati) and the Rishis of the north.

verses.sanskrit: एतद्द्वारं महाराज मानसस्य प्रकाशते। वर्षमस्य गिरेर्मध्ये रामेण श्रीमता कृतम्॥१२॥
verses.english: O great king, yonder appears the gate of Manaka. A gap was opened by Rama in the midst of this mountain.

verses.sanskrit: एष वातिकषण्डो वै प्रख्यातः सत्यविक्रमः। नात्यवर्तत यद्द्वारं विदेहादुत्तरं च यः॥१३॥
verses.english: O greatly powerful hero, here is the celebrated Vatikakhanda, which although near the gate of Vedika, lies on the north of it.

verses.sanskrit: इदमाश्चर्यमपरं देशेऽस्मिन्पुरुषर्षभ। क्षीणे युगे तु कौन्तेय शर्वस्य सह पार्षदैः॥१४॥
verses.english: O foremost of men, there is another very remarkable thing in connection with this place. It is this that at the end of every Yuga the deity Shiva who is capable of assuming every form at will may be seen here with Uma and his followers. In the yonder lake men, desirous of securing welfare to them, cheerfully gratify the wielder of Pinaka in the month of Chaitra by performing sacrifices.
verses.bhavadeepa: एष इति । यो रामः प्रख्यातः सत्यविक्रमश्च विदेहादुत्तरं च यद्वारं यद्वर्षस्य द्वारम् एषोऽनुभूयमानो वातिकषण्डो वातानीतः पद्मादिसमूहो नात्यवर्तत तेन रामेण कृतमिति पूर्वेणान्वयः । अनेन वायोरप्यस्मिन्वर्षे प्रवेशो नास्ति किमुतेतरस्येति पद्मादेर्वातानीतस्यात्राप्रवेशाद्रामसामर्थ्यं प्रत्यक्षमाश्चर्यमित्यर्थः ॥१३॥

verses.sanskrit: सहोमया च भवति दर्शनं कामरूपिणः। अस्मिन्सरसि सत्रैर्वै चैत्रे मासि पिनाकिनम्॥१५॥
verses.bhavadeepa: युगं पञ्चसंवत्सरात्मकं तस्मिन्क्षीणे समाप्ते सति यदा सौरसावनबार्हस्पत्यनाक्षत्रचान्द्राः संवत्सरा एककालं समाप्यन्ते स युगक्षयकालस्तस्मिन्नित्यर्थः । युगे क्षीणे इत्यस्य संवत्सरान्त इति वार्थः । चैत्रप्रतिपत् युगादिरिति व्यवहारात् ॥१४॥

verses.sanskrit: यजन्ते याजकाः सम्यक्परिवारं शुभार्थिनः। अत्रोपस्पृश्य सरसि श्रद्दधानो जितेन्द्रियः॥१६॥
verses.english: Bathing in Kalasa with devotion and with one's passions subdued, a man obtains the fruits of Agnishtoma sacrifice.
verses.bhavadeepa: अत एव पूर्वदिने शिवं दृष्ट्वा प्रतिपदमारभ्य मासमात्रं पिनाकिनं यजन्त इति संगच्छते ॥१५॥

verses.sanskrit: क्षीणपापः शुभाँल्लोकान्प्राप्नुते नात्र संशयः। एष उज्जानको नाम पावकिर्यत्र शान्तवान्। अरुंधतीसहायश्च वसिष्ठो भगवानृषिः॥१७॥
verses.english: The religious-minded and self-controlled men perform their ablations in this lake and become free from all sins. They certainly obtain the blessed regions. Here is the sacred Tirtha called Ujjanaka where the holy Rishi Vasishtha with his wife Arundhati lived.

verses.sanskrit: ह्रदश्च कुशवानेष यत्र पद्म कुशेशयम्। आश्रमश्चैव रुक्मिण्या यत्राशाम्यदकोपना॥१८॥
verses.english: Yonder is the lake called Kushavanisha in which grow the lotuses called Kushashaya. Here also is the hermitage of Rukmini where she attained peace by conquering her anger. O son of Pandu, O great king, you must have heard of the great hill Bhrigutunga. Behold it (now).
verses.bhavadeepa: पावकिः स्कन्दः शान्तवान् शमं प्राप । वसिष्ठोऽपि शान्तवान् ॥१७॥

verses.sanskrit: समाधीनां समासस्तु पाण्डवेय श्रुतस्त्वया। तं द्रक्ष्यसि महाराज भृगुतुङ्गं महागिरिम्॥१९॥
verses.bhavadeepa: कुशवान् जलवान् । ‘शरं वनं कुशं नीरम्’ इति धनंजयः । अकोपना जितक्रोधा ॥१८॥

verses.sanskrit: वितस्तां पश्य राजेन्द्र सर्वपापप्रमोचनीम्। महर्षिभिश्चाध्युषितां शीततोयां सुनिर्मलाम्॥२०॥
verses.english: O king of kings, behold Vitasta which cleanses all sins. The water of it is very cool and transparent and it is frequented by the great Rishis.

verses.sanskrit: जलां चोपजलां चैव यमुनामभितो नदीम्। उशीनरो वै यत्रेष्ट्वा वासवादत्यरिच्यत॥२१॥
verses.english: (Behold) Jala and Upjala the rivers on both the sides of the Yamuna. Ushinara surpassed Vasava (Indra in greatness) by performing a sacrifice here.

verses.sanskrit: तां देवसमितिं तस्य वासवश्च विशांपते। अभ्यागच्छन्नृपवरं ज्ञातुमग्निश्च भारत॥२२॥
verses.english: O king, O descendant of Bharata, being desirous of testing the merit of that great king, Vasava (Indra) and Agni came to his celestialslike Sava.

verses.sanskrit: जिज्ञासमानौ वरदौ महात्मानमुशीनरम्। इन्द्रः श्येनः कपोतोऽग्निर्भूत्वा यज्ञेऽभिजग्मतुः॥२३॥
verses.english: Being inquisitive to know Ushinara and being willing to bestow boons on him, those two celestials Indra and Agni, came to his sacrificial ground, Indra becoming a hawk and Agni a pigeon.

verses.sanskrit: ऊरू राज्ञः समासाद्य कपोतः श्येनजाद्भयात्। शरणार्थी तदा राजन्निलिल्ये भयपीडितः॥२४॥
verses.english: O king, the pigeon from the fear of the hawk fell upon the king's thighs for protection; and it became almost dead from the great fear.
